title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the previous page; the identifications of M and M_0 are my inference. E/S is an elliptic curve with 2 invertible. Σ_I ≃ E/(1,σ_E) is the P^1-bundle obtained as the quotient of E by the inversion. I is the finite étale scheme of degree 3 of non-zero 2-torsion points. M_0 is most likely E[2] and M most likely E[4]. A 'relative épinglage' is a section of the torsor P_M over End(M_0). Equivalently it is a trace-zero morphism (47) I → M lifting the inclusion I ⊂ M_0. Such a morphism automatically lands in M \ M_0. Composing with M ⊂ E → Σ_I gives (48) I → Δ_t.

What Δ_t is. For each non-zero 2-torsion point u, the points x with 2x = u form 4 points, which give 2 points modulo ±1. So Δ_t is the 6-point configuration in Σ_I of images of primitive 4-torsion points. Its canonical map f_t : Δ_t → I is étale of degree 2.

This page:
1. The lifting condition on (47) is equivalent to f_t ∘ (48) = id_I. That is, (48) is a section of Δ_t → I.
2. Δ_t is viewed as a fibre bundle of 'combinatorial octahedra': 6 vertices in 3 antipodal pairs indexed by I. A section picks one vertex from each antipodal pair, which is exactly a face of the octahedron (8 faces in all). Grothendieck writes and underlines 'face'.
3. Once such a face is given, the octahedron is 'I-épinglé'. It is then canonically isomorphic to the standard octahedron attached to I (and to μ_4^*, i.e. {0,∞}∪μ_4-type data, if the insertion is read correctly). This apparently holds without needing the biquadratic covering Σ_{I,2} of Σ_I. That covering is presumably the quotient by ±1 of multiplication by 2, a Galois (Z/2)^2 covering. Its fibres over the four branch points give the octahedron.

The page breaks off with '...'. The next page opens Chapter III, 'Épinglages de Legendre des courbes elliptiques'. So this is the bridge: lifts of an ordering of 2-torsion to 4-torsion, packaged as faces of an octahedron. It is the fibrewise, combinatorial avatar of the classical level-2 to level-4 passage (Legendre λ to Jacobi k, k' = √λ, √(1−λ), the biquadratic covering X(4) → X(2), with the octahedral S_4 symmetry of X(4)).
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The text is a fragment and breaks off mid-sentence.
Gap: it is not made explicit which of the 8 faces arise from trace-zero sections. If the trace condition singles out half of them (an alternating tetrahedral class), this is unstated on the page.

ideas.what: Sections of the degree-2 étale map from (4-torsion points of order 4)/± to the non-zero 2-torsion are viewed as faces of a combinatorial octahedron bundle over S.
ideas.modern_name: Octahedral configuration of 4-torsion images on E/±1; level-4 refinement of level-2 structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein's octahedral X(4); Jacobi's k, k'). The relative, combinatorial-scheme formulation is not specifically credited.

ideas.what: Relative épinglage, defined as a section of the torsor P_M over End(M_0), equivalently a trace-zero lift I → M.
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of lifts of level structure from E[2] to E[4]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard moduli theory of level structures (Katz–Mazur style)

ideas.what: The biquadratic covering Σ_{I,2} → Σ_I, i.e. the doubling map on E/±1.
ideas.modern_name: Lattès map / multiplication by 2 on the Kummer line

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine transitional fragment. It recasts the choice of 4-torsion lifts of 2-torsion as choosing a face of an octahedron bundle, preparing the 'Legendre épinglages' chapter. The underlying mathematics (octahedral level-4 configuration, k = √λ) is classical. The combinatorial packaging is pleasant but not substantive enough to be a missed result.
transcription_corrections: '(48) définit une forme des fibrés en octaèdres' should read '(48) définit une face (underlined) du/des fibré(s) en octaèdres combinatoires Δ_t sur S'.
'Dans ce cas l'octaèdre en I —' is more likely 'Dans ce cas l'octaèdre est I-épinglé'. The 'I —' at the line end continues as '-épinglé' on the next line.
'il est can. isomorphe au [-?-] octaèdre' has a struck-out letter before 'octaèdre'. The text likely reads 'canoniquement isomorphe à l'octaèdre standard défini par I'.
'[?] prenant' is probably 'sans prendre' (or '(sans prendre'): '...défini par I, sans prendre le revêtement biquadratique Σ_{I,2} de Σ_I...'.
The inserted line above 'I,' reads roughly 'et les sections de μ_4^*'. The reading is uncertain; the symbol could be μ_4 with an asterisk marking a note.
